To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) conservatism is a pervasive feature of modern financial reporting, (2) it is not a relic of the past but has increased over time, (3) it cannot be explained as a byproduct of earnings management, the abandonment option, or the tax code, and (4) the contracting, shareholder litigation and accounting regulation explanations are important but do not explain the full extent of conservatism.
(1) conservatism in accounting is pervasive, (2) conservatism has increased over time, and (3) the increase in conservatism is not due solely to the abandonment option.

1) the evidence on the existence and magnitude of conservatism is robust and suggests conservatism has increased over time; 2) the evidence on conservatism's explanations is mixed, but suggests that contracting, shareholder litigation and taxation all contribute to conservatism; and 3) the evidence on earnings management and the abandonment explanation is mixed, but the evidence does not support these explanations as primary explanations for conservatism.
